key_insight: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach effectively by judging actions after their consequences are visible.
engineering_relevance: Use retrospective action-level feedback to improve agent policies rather than selecting teachers solely by their own task success.
method: Compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld.
Judge complete trajectories by asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed.
Use JEV as a reinforcement-learning teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop.
evidence_signal: JEV teaching improved Qwen2.5-1.5B success over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop.
watch_item: Teacher results cover one teacher and two benchmarks; retrospective judging also requires completed trajectories.
paper_title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
